asks.title: What the root has to get right
asks.text: What feels wrong or missing in that story and the proposed root, given your chosen sentence about being unfinished and running when the sky clears?
asks.picture: After a trip under the red storm, a colonist comes home with a scan and useful tissue, but starts changing. Later the cloud opens and the colony rushes between shelters.
asks.decision: F1/F2: a list of grotesque creatures and mechanics could still miss why the place is worth entering and frightening to inhabit.
asks.why: F1/F2: a list of grotesque creatures and mechanics could still miss why the place is worth entering and frightening to inhabit.
asks.guess: The weather and bodily cost lead; expeditions give the player a reason to accept that danger. I recommend making those the through-line.
asks.tree_changes: If the costly expedition leads, reorder the root and connect its success to lasting bodily consequences. If living under the sky clock leads, begin with ordinary colony work repeatedly interrupted by the sky. If unfinished life itself leads, begin with its visible cycles. All built branches remain covered. A correction changes dependent claims; silence approves nothing.

asks.title: The first demonstration
asks.text: Which demonstration would you put first, and what single failure in it would make you stop the review?
asks.picture: A: ordinary workers notice the tells and shelter through a Burn, followed by a touched patient being treated. B: a genome expedition ends with a matched natural part being installed. C: a dangerous scan fills a Helix contract. D: a growing Coalescence is deliberately caught by a forced Burn. These are separate candidate demonstrations.
asks.decision: F1/F2/F3: the owner-chosen experience is on record, but a flagship pick and concrete rejection case are not.
asks.why: F1/F2/F3: the owner-chosen experience is on record, but a flagship pick and concrete rejection case are not.
asks.guess: A first: show that the sky is dangerous and that what happens to people matters. I recommend B and C as distinct later scenes, with D proving its own threat and payoff.
asks.tree_changes: The pick binds showcase 1 only after a real owner decision. The stated failure becomes a candidate acceptance requirement. Other capabilities retain separate scenes; later showcases must add different functionality, and ordinary checks cover the remainder. Root approval alone never becomes a flagship pick.

asks.title: What a useful Burn lets you attempt
asks.text: What should a well-prepared traveller be able to get done between those shelters before the light becomes too costly?
asks.picture: A prepared colonist has a roofed refuge on each side of a red clearing. During the Bloom a predator and the fog make crossing dangerous. The Burn clears the shot and drives UV-shy creatures inward, while Scaldhides remain outside and the traveller takes exposure.
asks.decision: F1: the older sheet calls the Burn a travel window while your chosen line says run. Both can be true, but a harmless sunny interval or an unusable trap would miss the tension.
asks.why: F1: the older sheet calls the Burn a travel window while your chosen line says run. Both can be true, but a harmless sunny interval or an unusable trap would miss the tension.
asks.guess: One purposeful dash or a brief rescue, paid for by exposure, rather than routine safe outdoor work. I recommend a crossing that is clearly worse for an unprepared traveller.
asks.tree_changes: A brief dash needs measured distance, shelters, injury and mutation exposure in one crossing scene. A rescue needs a carrying case and enough time for the return. A longer sortie needs a longer exposure-budget demonstration. An emergency-only picture changes how the root describes the tactical window while retaining the lifted fog and existing weapon behavior.

asks.title: Enough warning to make a decision
asks.text: When the sky opens, which people should reasonably have reached safety, and what should the distant work party know before the colony starts its own Burn?
asks.picture: A forty-colonist settlement is spread between a workshop, a near field and a distant work party. Gawpsacks sink and Rattlegropes shake. A natural Burn follows; the current lead is about twenty seconds at normal speed. In a separate case, a warmed Repulsor starts a whole-map Burn without that natural tell sequence.
asks.decision: F1/F3: a cue can exist without giving a useful choice, and forced whole-map weather can surprise people far from the machine.
asks.why: F1/F3: a cue can exist without giving a useful choice, and forced whole-map weather can surprise people far from the machine.
asks.guess: People near a planned refuge can shelter; a remote expedition may have to improvise. I recommend an honest indication that switching the Repulsor affects everyone on the map.
asks.tree_changes: Near-refuge safety sets a warning-window case with ordinary walking. Recall of the distant party requires longer lead or a planned remote refuge and a demonstration. A clear device-state explanation adds an interface requirement; a pre-activation warning adds a distinct forced-Burn scene. No automatic rescue or immunity is inferred.

asks.title: The warning before the body changes
asks.text: Before the first new body part or harmful change appears, what should make you decide this worker needs treatment now?
asks.picture: A worker spends time outside in the Bloom and then goes indoors. The current build keeps the touched condition; later it can grow another mutation. A Sunbeam stops that progression, leaves existing changes and gives no future protection, as already ruled.
asks.decision: F2/F3: hidden accumulation can turn the ruled danger into a surprise punishment. A health entry alone may not be enough in a large colony.
asks.why: F2/F3: hidden accumulation can turn the ruled danger into a surprise punishment. A health entry alone may not be enough in a large colony.
asks.guess: A readable early health state and a noticeable transition to active change, without repeated letters for every tiny exposure. I recommend judging the first warning and the next action together.
asks.tree_changes: If the health panel is sufficient, require an intelligible progression state and no extra alert. If a visible symptom matters, define it through a labelled mock before visual acceptance. If an alert matters, bind a threshold and repetition rule. Existing exposure, arrest, persistence and reinfection behavior are not being offered for removal.

asks.title: An expedition that earns its wait
asks.text: What has to come home from that trip for it to feel like progress worth another expedition?
asks.picture: A colonist needs a natural leg. The team injects that colonist's genome into a Bloody Mess and comes back four days later. The host dies producing a matched batch of ordinary organs and limbs, but this batch has no leg. This is the current random batch, not a proposed targeted-growth machine.
asks.decision: F2: the one-use host is already ruled, but useful output and the cost of reaching and returning to it need a player-facing bar.
asks.why: F2: the one-use host is already ruled, but useful output and the cost of reaching and returning to it need a player-facing bar.
asks.guess: Other genuinely useful or sellable matched tissue can make a failed leg roll worthwhile, provided the risk and return trip are readable. I recommend judging the whole expedition rather than the instant batch spawn.
asks.tree_changes: A useful mixed haul needs a representative batch and a clear use or sale after return. Progress toward this patient's specific recovery needs a defined route beyond hoping at the next host; any added route must be argued separately. A very harsh lottery needs that cost signalled before commitment. The one-use host, normal mixed batch and sellable output remain built coverage.

asks.title: A bargain you notice after surgery
asks.text: What ordinary task should make you feel the price of that better fighter, and how disruptive should that price be during the following day?
asks.picture: A brawler fitted with a Pillar Arm wins a fight that a natural arm would have lost, then returns to an ordinary day of work and meals. Its clumsy manipulation, weight and extra hunger are already built. All five unusual limbs are built; removing one releases an Unfinished.
asks.decision: F2/F3: a positive stat and a negative stat can coexist while the limb still plays as a free upgrade. The lasting costs are promised; their felt size remains provisional.
asks.why: F2/F3: a positive stat and a negative stat can coexist while the limb still plays as a free upgrade. The lasting costs are promised; their felt size remains provisional.
asks.guess: It should force a real reassignment away from skilled hand work, plus a food burden, without making the pawn useless. I recommend comparing one unchanged day before surgery with one after.
asks.tree_changes: A changed work role makes work completion and reassignment the acceptance example. A resource burden makes food and walking costs part of it. Frequent disruption needs an appropriate event case for the affected limb. The gain remains; tune and prove the lasting cost. No new requirement is derived for every stat, and no limb is offered for removal.

asks.title: The reason to stop a Coalescence growing
asks.text: What should make waiting for one more stage a difficult choice for a colony that can already handle the current attackers?
asks.picture: A Coalescence grows through a long Bloom. More Unfinished walk into it; it sends mad ones out. The colony could start the Repulsor now, or wait for a larger collapse and more tissue. Its emitted manhunter count is currently capped, so a higher stage can become merely a better payout behind the same defense.
asks.decision: F1/F2: staged mass and a sample formula can pass while the giant never changes a decision. The cost of waiting needs to be concrete.
asks.why: F1/F2: staged mass and a sample formula can pass while the giant never changes a decision. The cost of waiting needs to be concrete.
asks.guess: More pressure on access to the site and on the workers who must recover the tissue, rather than a consequence unrelated to the creature. I recommend showing the same colony at two stages.
asks.tree_changes: If stronger attacks are the pressure, demonstrate the changed threat at the same defense. If access is the pressure, show the threatened route and recovery trip. If waiting is meant to be a reward for containing it, require meaningful containment and retain bounded emissions. The growth, absorption, Burn collapse and payout remain independent promises.

failure_modes: F1 — The sky changes color but does not create an intelligible decision: tells are late/unreadable, shelter disagrees with what is drawn, or ordinary sun-seeking hides the Burn response. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:10; src/RimMandrake/Contagion/Source/RM_GameCondition_ContagionBurn.cs; ITEM:CONTAGION_SUNDASH_DECIDE_UNDER_THE_BLOOM.

F2 — Unfinished biology becomes a static grotesque zoo or a free factory: exposure is opaque, mutation or chosen surgery is a net upgrade, matched tissue feels generic, scans are chores, or the Coalescence has no costly choice. Sources: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_contagion.md; ITEM:CONTAGION_GENOME_ORGAN_GROWING_1; ITEM:CONTAGION_GPT_ENRICHMENT_1.

F3 — A mechanism-only pass hides a failed player journey: forced counters/severity substitute for approach, waiting, use and aftermath; settings, reload, colony scale, death traces or actual surgery fail without a readable sign. Sources: src/RimMandrake/Contagion/validation.py; src/RimMandrake/rimflow/roles/designer_scene_contract.md; ITEM:CONTAGION_REVIEW_STAGE_JUDGE_LOOKS_FIRST.

neighbours.text: Runtime package is mandrake.rm.biomes, not dev folder About package. Tests and MayRequire must use actual composed identities.
Hard assembly dependency supplies scaled acid explosion, stage-scaled render subworker and scripted creep die-off. Birth uses a wrapper, not duplicated explosion code.

Existing Direct Sun escape and shade service can compete with Coalescence walking and Burn dive. Burn still uses its exact-cell roof/water/tree predicate. Existing sundash item is an integration decision, not permission for another sun.
Linked search/reset/scope presentation already used; no new settings framework needed.
Optional guarded floating and fission retained for bulloo/zhool; do not confuse permanent floating with short flight stat or new code owed in this mod.
RustPuff is a guarded roster dependency; Shambles moved to TheRot. Neither is an absent Contagion creature to rebuild.
Creep defs reside here, while the border die-off mechanic belongs to Forge. Package location is not feature ownership.
Common family loot/weathering/deconstruction and local-map scatter consume this biome's eroded children. No planet generator proposed.
FindMod-guarded payload registers strings/targets with the existing scanner; this biome does not own another scanner.
Helix faction attachment, Spire and Ashfall Research Base plot/dungeon are distinct ownership. No generic mod question asks the owner to re-design their campaign role.

Natural body-part restoration already supports the matched-arm/leg loop. Ordinary surgery, hediff parts/verbs, CompHatcher, quest parts and force-weather provide existing mechanisms; do not invent replacements.

root_draft.speaker: agent
root_draft.text: The Contagion is a mutation engine under a red storm: the landscape keeps making unfinished life, and a visit can leave a colonist unfinished too. The player reads the Gawpsacks sinking and the Rattlegropes shaking, then makes a costly choice when the cloud tears: reach shelter, or use the lifted fog while UV-shy life retreats and armored predators remain outside. Exposure brings unwanted changes; a Sunbeam can stop the current progression, but cannot undo what grew or protect the next trip. The same biology offers reasons to venture in: a Bloody Mess can consume itself growing donor-matched organs and natural limbs, short-lived Unfinished can be scanned for Helix contracts, and a Coalescence left through a long Bloom becomes a growing threat whose Burn collapse yields unusual tissue. Deliberately installed grown limbs exchange an ability for a lasting cost, with danger again when removed. Flesh-like plants, flying skin creatures, drifting gas sacs and the traces of death make this a living place rather than a red ordinary forest. The biome offers no forage; sterile mulch is a practical reward. These connected promises need separate demonstrations of the sky, bodily consequences and expeditions.

failure_mode_sources.text: F1 — The sky changes color but does not create an intelligible decision: tells are late/unreadable, shelter disagrees with what is drawn, or ordinary sun-seeking hides the Burn response. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md:10; src/RimMandrake/Contagion/Source/RM_GameCondition_ContagionBurn.cs; ITEM:CONTAGION_SUNDASH_DECIDE_UNDER_THE_BLOOM.

F2 — Unfinished biology becomes a static grotesque zoo or a free factory: exposure is opaque, mutation or chosen surgery is a net upgrade, matched tissue feels generic, scans are chores, or the Coalescence has no costly choice. Sources: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_contagion.md; ITEM:CONTAGION_GENOME_ORGAN_GROWING_1; ITEM:CONTAGION_GPT_ENRICHMENT_1.

F3 — A mechanism-only pass hides a failed player journey: forced counters/severity substitute for approach, waiting, use and aftermath; settings, reload, colony scale, death traces or actual surgery fail without a readable sign. Sources: src/RimMandrake/Contagion/validation.py; src/RimMandrake/rimflow/roles/designer_scene_contract.md; ITEM:CONTAGION_REVIEW_STAGE_JUDGE_LOOKS_FIRST.
